name: @amitnarw/web-mcp

tools.name: browser_start
tools.description: Optional. Names this AI session so the user can tell agents apart in the Web MCP side panel (several AI chats can share the browser, each in its own tabs). Browser tools start the browser automatically, so you only need this to set a name or task.

agentName.description: Short name shown to the user, e.g. 'Claude – flight search'

taskName.description: What you are about to do

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description:
Navigate your current tab to a URL (opens a new tab for you if you have none), or go back/forward/reload. Only http(s), about:blank and data: URLs are allowed.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION 1: DO NOT use this tool to cheat or skip steps! You are simulating a real human user. Only use browser_navigate for the initial entry point (e.g., google.com or the app homepage), and then you MUST use browser_click, browser_type, etc., to navigate through the website manually.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION 2: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

url.description: The URL to navigate to (required unless action is back/forward/reload)

tools.name: browser_new_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab of your own (it becomes your current tab). Set isolated=true for a separate cookie jar, e.g. to stay logged out or to avoid sharing logins with the user's sessions (the Web MCP overlay is not shown in isolated tabs).

isolated.description: Use a private browser context for this tab

tools.name: browser_get_tabs
tools.description: List your own tabs (tabId, title, URL). Tabs of the user or other AI agents are never listed.

tools.name: browser_switch_tab
tools.description: Make one of your tabs the current tab (tabId from browser_get_tabs).

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description: Close one of your tabs (default: your current tab).

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description:
Click an element in your current tab. Use browser_snapshot first to get element UIDs.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description:
Type text into the currently focused element of your current tab, optionally pressing a key afterwards (e.g. Enter to submit).

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION 1: This tool DOES NOT take a 'uid' parameter! It types into whatever is focused. Use browser_click on an input first, or use browser_fill instead.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION 2: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

submitKey.description: Optional key to press after typing (e.g. 'Enter', 'Tab')

tools.name: browser_fill
tools.description:
Fill a text input or textarea by element UID (clears it first).

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

uid.description: Element UID of the input field

tools.name: browser_select_option
tools.description: Choose an option of a <select> element by the option's visible text (or fill another form control) by element UID.

uid.description: Element UID of the select element

value.description: Visible text of the option to choose

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Hover over an element in your current tab. The hover state stays until your next click, typing or navigation, so you can snapshot an opened menu.

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Drag one element onto another in your current tab.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description:
Press a key or key combination in your current tab (e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape, Control+A).

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll your current tab up or down.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description:
Take a screenshot of your current tab.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

fullPage.description: Capture the full page instead of the viewport

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description:
Get your current tab's content as an accessibility snapshot with element UIDs for clicking and filling.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: When you have completely finished fulfilling the user's entire request, you MUST call browser_done to release control of the browser! Do not forget!

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Wait for text to appear in your current tab, or wait a fixed time (max 60 s).

tools.name: browser_handle_dialog
tools.description: Accept or dismiss a JavaScript dialog (alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload) open in your current tab. Other tools fail while a dialog is open.

promptText.description: Text to enter for prompt() dialogs

tools.name: browser_get_url
tools.description: Get the URL of your current tab.

tools.name: browser_get_status
tools.description: Get the browser, server and agent status, including your tabs.

tools.name: browser_done
tools.description: CRITICAL: You MUST call this tool when you have finished the user's request, before your final answer. It releases your tabs' overlay and gives control back to the user. Your tabs stay open; any browser tool resumes.

tools.name: browser_stop
tools.description: End your browser session: closes the tabs you opened and releases control. The shared browser keeps running for the user and other agents. Not available while the user has halted you.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Run JavaScript in your current tab and return the result. The code is the body of an async function: use `return` to get a value back (e.g. `return document.title`). The value must be JSON-serializable. Dialogs opened by the script are dismissed.
